RIDGEWAY CAR RENTAL - RATE CARD AND FEE POLICY
Downtown and Airport branches. Effective 1 August 2026. All amounts include sales tax and airport concession recovery; nothing is added at checkout except the items listed here.

DAILY AND WEEKLY RATES
- Economy: $44 per day, $265 per week
- Compact: $48 per day, $289 per week
- Midsize: $57 per day, $342 per week
- Minivan: $83 per day, $498 per week
A rental day is 24 hours from the pickup time. Weekly rates apply to rentals of 5 to 7 days.

EXTENSIONS AND LATE RETURNS
- Extensions arranged by phone or app before the original return time are billed at the contract's daily rate for each extra day, plus any per-day extras on the contract for those days.

PER-DAY EXTRAS
- Additional driver: $13 per day

SQCC-CTX-2.title: Brightline Fibre residential billing guide v4.2
SQCC-CTX-2.text:
BRIGHTLINE FIBRE - RESIDENTIAL BILLING GUIDE
Version 4.2, updated June 2026. For customer-care agents and customers.

1. How bills work
Bills are issued on the 1st of each month and cover the coming month in advance. Payment is due on the 5th of that month (the due date). For billing purposes every month is treated as 30 days long, whatever the calendar says.

2. Plans (monthly, taxes included)
- Fibre 300: $57
- Fibre 900: $84
- Fibre 2G: $112
- Voice line add-on: $9
Router rental is included in every plan.

3. Changing plans mid-month
Upgrades take effect the same day. The next bill includes (a) the new plan for the coming month and (b) a one-off adjustment for the rest of the current month: the difference between the new and old monthly price x (days remaining / 30). The day of the change counts as a day on the new plan, so a change on the 21st leaves 10 days (the 21st through the 30th). Downgrades take effect on the 1st of the next month with no adjustment.

4. Equipment
- Wi-Fi extender rental: $6 per extender per month. Maximum of 3 extenders per account.
- Replacement router (lost or damaged): $95 one-off.
- Unreturned equipment after cancellation: $95 per router, $40 per extender.

5. Late payment
- If any balance is still unpaid 21 days after the due date, a $10 late fee is added.
- At the same point, a late payment charge of 5% of the overdue balance is added.
- Neither applies if the balance is paid within 21 days of the due date. Agents may waive the $10 late fee once per 12 months as a goodwill gesture; the 5% charge cannot be waived.

6. Moving home
Moves within our network are free with 14 days' notice. Moves outside our network count as cancellation.

7. Cancelling
30 days' notice. The final bill is prorated to the cancellation date using the 30-day rule above. No early-termination fee on monthly plans; 18-month contract plans pay $15 for each remaining month.

8. Service credits
Outages over 24 hours earn a credit of 1/30 of the monthly plan price per full day, applied on request.
SQCC-CTX-2.notes: SQCC-002 (consistent): upgrade 300 -> 900 on the 11th: 20 days on the new plan (11th-30th, 30-day month); (84 - 57) x 20/30 = 18; bill = 84 + 18 = 102, correct. The worked example in section 3 deliberately uses the 21st, not the 11th. SQCC-003 (discrepancy): 2 extenders x $6 = $12; maximum 3 per account = $18; the stated $30 implies 5 extenders: does not reconcile; router is included, so no router fee explains it. SQCC-004 (consistent): paid 25 days after the due date (> 21) so the $10 late fee and 5% x 84 = 4.20 both apply; the customer's '30 days' is wrong; waiving the $10 once is optional goodwill, not an admission of error.

If a dues payment fails we retry after 3 days. A second failure adds an $8 admin fee and suspends check-in until the balance is cleared.

Questions: members@harborloft.example or the front desk at either location.

SQLEC-CTX-1.title: ECON 110 week 6 handout: price elasticity of demand
SQLEC-CTX-1.text:
ECON 110 - PRINCIPLES OF MICROECONOMICS
Week 6 handout: price elasticity of demand. Prof. R. Ansbach, Fall 2026.

Course admin (reminder)
- Grade weights: problem sets 30%, midterm 30%, final exam 40%. Your problem-set score is the average of your best 8 of 10 sets.
- Final exam: Thursday 10 December, 9:00-12:00, Hollingworth Hall. A formula sheet is provided.
- Office hours move to Tuesday 2-4 pm this week only.

1. Definition
Price elasticity of demand (PED) measures how strongly quantity demanded responds to a change in price:
PED = (% change in quantity demanded) / (% change in price).
PED is negative for normal demand curves; we usually talk about its absolute value.
- |PED| > 1: elastic (quantity responds more than proportionally)
- |PED| = 1: unit elastic
- |PED| < 1: inelastic

2. Why we use the midpoint (arc) method
Simple percentage changes depend on the direction you measure in: going from 10 to 12 is +20%, but going back from 12 to 10 is -16.7%. The midpoint method divides each change by the AVERAGE of the start and end values, so the answer is the same in both directions:
% change in Q = (Q2 - Q1) / ((Q1 + Q2) / 2)
% change in P = (P2 - P1) / ((P1 + P2) / 2)
Use the midpoint method on problem sets and exams unless a question says otherwise.

3. Worked example
Coffee kiosk: price rises from $3.00 to $3.50, cups sold per day fall from 400 to 360.
% change in Q = -40 / 380 = -10.5%
% change in P = 0.50 / 3.25 = 15.4%
PED = -0.68, so demand is inelastic. Revenue rises from $1,200 to $1,260.

4. Estimates from the readings (Aldmere Transit Study; fictional data for class use)
- City bus ridership, short run (first year after a fare change): -0.3
- City bus ridership, long run (after five years): -0.7
- Cinema tickets: -1.6
- Cigarettes: -0.4
Long-run demand is more elastic because people have time to find substitutes (move closer to work, buy a bike, car-pool).

5. Elasticity and total revenue
If demand is elastic, a price increase reduces total revenue; if it is inelastic, a price increase raises total revenue.

6. Common mistakes
Mixing up percentage points and percent; forgetting the negative sign; using simple percentage changes when the midpoint method is asked for.
SQLEC-CTX-1.notes: SQLEC-001: midpoint: dQ = -300 / 1,050 = -28.57%; dP = 10 / 45 = 22.22%; PED = -1.29, elastic (revenue 48,000 -> 45,000). Trap: simple percentages give -25% / +25% = -1.0, 'unit elastic'. SQLEC-002: weights 30/30/40: 0.3 x 91 + 0.3 x 72 = 48.9; (80 - 48.9) / 0.4 = 77.75. Trap: equal weights give 77; 'best 8 of 10' is noise because the student states the average. SQLEC-003 (lookup): long-run bus ridership -0.7; the short-run -0.3 is the neighbouring-row trap.

Benefits
- Medical, dental and vision from day one; employee premium 10%.
- 401(k) with 4% match, immediate vesting (not included in any compensation total).
- 25 days PTO plus 10 public holidays.
- $1,500 annual learning budget.

Logistics
- Location: Wharf Street office, hybrid, 2 days a week on site. Candidate lives locally; no relocation package applies.
- Target start date: 2 November 2026. Background check in progress.
- Offer expires 9 October 2026.

Approval notes
- Band for level: $128,000-$158,000 base. Option B sits near the top of the band; the hiring manager prefers Option A.
- Any sign-on above $15,000 or equity above $60,000 needs VP approval (Grete Solberg).
- Candidate's current package (as told to the recruiter): $118,000 base plus about 6% bonus.

Interview feedback summary
Strong on streaming pipelines and cost optimisation; weaker on stakeholder communication per panel 3. Hire recommendation: yes.

Traps: counting the whole 60,000 grant in year one (234,040 / 239,160), counting only the first 9,000 sign-on part (183,040), applying 12% to Option B (200,240), adding the 401(k) match (explicitly excluded) or relocation (does not apply). SQREC-003 (consistent): letter first-year cash 174,040 = 142,000 + 17,040 + 15,000 sign-on; the candidate's 159,040 omits the sign-on; the letter is right.

SQSALES-CTX-1.title: Kestrel Fieldworks cold-chain monitoring price sheet
SQSALES-CTX-1.text:
KESTREL FIELDWORKS - COLD-CHAIN MONITORING
Price sheet for US customers, revision 2026-07. All prices USD, excluding sales tax.

HARDWARE (one-time)
- KG-4 gateway hub: $540 each. One hub supports up to 24 sensors of any type. Hubs talk over the building's own network and cannot serve sensors in a different building, so every building (site) needs its own hub or hubs.
- TS-2 temperature and humidity sensor: $78 each.
- DS-1 door-open sensor: $34 each. Door sensors count toward a hub's 24-sensor capacity.
- Replacement batteries (4-pack): $19.

INSTALLATION (one-time)
- Standard installation: $1,200 per site. Covers mounting and commissioning of up to 2 hubs and all of their sensors.
- Each additional hub at the same site: $150 installation.
- After-hours installation (evenings or weekends), only when requested: add 25% to the installation price.

MONITORING SUBSCRIPTION (recurring)
Billed monthly per active sensor. Every account includes its first 10 sensors at no monitoring charge; the rate below applies to each sensor above those 10. The rate is set by the account's TOTAL sensor count and applies to every billable sensor (it is not graduated).
- 1 to 100 sensors on the account: $5.50 per billable sensor per month
- 101 to 250 sensors: $4.75 per billable sensor per month
- 251 or more sensors: $4.00 per billable sensor per month
Annual prepay: 5% off monitoring when the full year is paid up front. Monthly billing has no discount.

OPTIONAL ADD-ONS (recurring)
- Cellular backup: $9 per hub per month.
- Extended data retention (7 years instead of 2): $40 per account per month.
- SMS alert bundle beyond 500 messages: $12 per additional 500.

WARRANTY AND SUPPORT
Hubs and sensors carry a 3-year limited warranty. Sensors that fail calibration inside warranty are replaced at no charge; we cover shipping one way. Support is by email and phone, 7 am to 7 pm Central, Monday to Saturday; critical temperature alerts are routed 24/7.

CONTRACT NOTES
Quotes are valid for 30 days. Hardware ships within 10 business days of order. Monitoring begins on the day each sensor is first commissioned and is billed in full for that month. Sensors removed from service stop billing from the next calendar month once they are decommissioned in the dashboard.
SQSALES-CTX-1.notes: SQSALES-001: hubs cannot be shared across buildings: warehouse 50 sensors -> 3 hubs, annex 14+8=22 -> 1 hub (pooling 72 sensors would wrongly give 3). Door sensors count toward capacity. Installation 2 x 1,200 + 1 extra warehouse hub x 150 = 2,550. First 10 sensors per ACCOUNT free; tier set by total (72 -> $5.50, not graduated); monthly billing so the 5% prepay discount does NOT apply; after-hours surcharge only if requested. Year one = 9,974 one-time + 341 x 12 = 14,066. SQSALES-002 (discrepancy): 41 sensors, one site, no add-ons -> 31 billable x 5.50 = 170.50/month; even ignoring the free 10 the maximum is 225.50; the stated 286 equals 52 billable sensors (62 sensors) and does not reconcile.

SQSALES-CTX-2.title: Lumenpath order form terms and Q4 2026 price schedule
SQSALES-CTX-2.text:
LUMENPATH - ORDER FORM TERMS AND PRICE SCHEDULE
Field-team scheduling platform. Valid for orders signed 1 October to 31 December 2026. USD.

PLANS
- Team: $32 per seat per month, minimum 10 seats, monthly or annual billing.
- Business: $49 per seat per month, minimum 35 seats, billed annually in advance (seat price x 12 x seats). If fewer than 35 seats are ordered, the invoice is for 35.
- Enterprise: custom pricing, minimum 250 seats.
Seats can be added mid-term and are prorated to the term end date. Seats cannot be reduced until renewal.

ONE-TIME ONBOARDING
- Team: self-serve, no charge.
- Business: $4,500 for accounts up to 60 seats; $6,000 for 61 seats or more. Onboarding is charged once, at the start of the first term, and is never discounted.

MULTI-YEAR TERMS (Business and Enterprise)
- 2-year term: 6% off the seat price for the whole term.
- 3-year term: 12% off the seat price for the whole term, and the discounted seat price is locked for all three years.
Multi-year terms are still invoiced one year at a time.

OTHER DISCOUNTS
- Registered nonprofits and schools: 8% off the seat price.
- Discounts do not stack. Where more than one discount applies, only the single largest one is used.

ADD-ONS (annual, Business and Enterprise)
- EU data residency: $3,200 per year per account.
- Advanced routing: $6 per seat per month.
- Premium support (1-hour response): 15% of annual seat fees.

RENEWALS
Renewals are quoted at the list price in effect on the renewal date, plus any add-ons active at that time. One-year renewals of accounts still on the 2025 price schedule are capped at a 7% increase per seat.

PAYMENT
Invoices are due Net 30. Card payments carry no surcharge. Late balances accrue 1% per month after 15 days' notice.

SERVICE
Uptime target 99.9% measured monthly; service credits are described in the Service Level Addendum, not in this form. Customer data is exported on request within 10 business days of termination.
SQSALES-CTX-2.notes: Chain c01: 38 seats Business 1-year = 38 x 49 x 12 = 22,344 + 4,500 onboarding = 26,844; 3-year: 49 x 0.88 = 43.12 -> 517.44/seat/yr x 38 = 19,662.72/yr x 3 = 58,988.16 + 4,500 once (never discounted) = 63,488.16; drop to 34 seats -> Business minimum 35 is invoiced -> 35 x 517.44 x 3 = 54,331.20 + 4,500 = 58,831.20. SQSALES-006: discounts do not stack; nonprofit 8% beats 2-year 6% -> 49 x 0.92 = 45.08 (stacked 42.14 / compounded 42.38 are wrong). SQSALES-007 (consistent): renewal 40 seats x 588 = 23,520 + EU data residency 3,200 = 26,720, the quote is correct. Noise: 7% renewal cap (applies to 2025-schedule accounts only), premium support 15%, advanced routing.

SQTEAM-CTX-1.title: Platform team Q3 budget and tooling review notes
SQTEAM-CTX-1.text:
PLATFORM TEAM - Q3 BUDGET AND TOOLING REVIEW
Notes, 24 September 2026. Present: Hollis (lead), Marguerite, Dev, Oyelaran, Sunniva. Notes by Sunniva.

1. Contractor spend (Halvorsen Data)
- Q3 contractor budget: $96,000 (July to September).
- Rate: Halvorsen first quoted $124/hour; we signed at $118/hour in the July 8 SOW.
- July invoice: $31,400 (paid).
- August invoice: $28,750 (paid). Breakdown on the invoice: 220 hours at the SOW rate plus the fixed-fee warehouse migration of $2,790 that Hollis approved in July.
- September invoice not received yet. Halvorsen's own estimate is about $22,000.
- Hollis: no new contractor work starts before October without a budget check.

2. Cloud spend
- Annual cloud budget $240,000. Spend January to August: $153,600. Dev flagged the storage line rising 4% month on month since May.
- Action: Dev to tag the three untagged staging clusters by Oct 3.

3. CI tooling proposal (Pipewright)
- Oyelaran presented Pipewright to replace the self-hosted runners.
- Cost: $18,000 one-time setup and migration, then $1,250 per month subscription.
- Expected saving: about 60 engineer-hours per month of runner maintenance and flaky-build triage. Finance's loaded engineering cost for planning is $85/hour.
- Marguerite asked for a payback estimate before the October planning meeting. Decision deferred.

4. Hiring
- One backend req approved for Q4; the posting goes live Oct 6. Panel: Hollis, Dev, Marguerite.

5. On-call
- Rota changes from weekly to 4-day shifts starting Oct 13. Sunniva to update the pager schedule.

6. Office move
- Floor 5 move is Nov 2-3. Everyone packs desks by Oct 31.

Action items
- Sunniva: circulate these notes; update the pager schedule.
- Dev: tag staging clusters; storage cost breakdown.
- Oyelaran: Pipewright payback estimate; confirm SSO support.
- Hollis: confirm the September Halvorsen invoice with finance when it lands.
SQTEAM-CTX-1.notes: SQTEAM-001 (lookup): signed rate $118/hour; $124 was only the first quote. SQTEAM-002: saving 60 x 85 = 5,100/month minus 1,250 subscription = 3,850 net; payback 18,000 / 3,850 = 4.68 months (ignoring the subscription gives 3.53; 18,000/1,250 = 14.4 is meaningless). SQTEAM-003 (discrepancy): 96,000 - 31,400 - 28,750 = 35,850 left before September; about 13,850 after the ~22,000 estimate; 'about fifty K left' does not reconcile. SQTEAM-004 (consistent): 220 x 118 = 25,960 + 2,790 approved migration fee = 28,750, the invoice is correct. Noise: cloud spend 153,600 of 240,000, hiring, on-call, office move.
